Your Honour, the killings aren't disputed, but when one looks at the scale of them and the type of people who were killed, it wasn't just the men and the men of fighting age, but old men, babies, as in the Hrustovo garage killings which took place. Your Honours may recall, because you visited the site, where the Velegici school took -- was stood, but stands no longer, and the graveyard that now stands there. I'm going to, Your Honours, just to look at one photograph that was taken. I know that Your Honours walked around it and saw the grave. It should be added that the bodies were not recovered there. They were recovered from other exhumation sites, and reburied at a later stage. Your Honour, it's not the clearest, but you can see that one of the stones relates to a Mr. Arif Pasic who was born in - as I say, it's not the clearest - but actually 1912, and died in 1992 at the age of 80. Thank you. Thank you, usher. You can take that away. Your Honour, evidence of the rapes was all given in closed session or by way of transcript evidence or statement under the provisions of Rule 92 bis. Your Honours, may I simply ask Your Honours perhaps to read the evidence of BT-33, who testified, and the statements of BT-71, 74, and 75, in particular, the last. Your Honours, the repetition of all these events across the 13 municipalities from which the Prosecution has called evidence, we submit, cannot as a matter of experience and of common sense come about through coincidence, through happenstance, through individual renegade municipalities off on a course of their own without any sort of coordinating and background plan and instruction. We would invite Your Honours to look at what BT-19, who we commend to Your Honours as the most impressive of the witnesses who came from outside the area, the so-called internationals, what he had to say about this, at pages -- transcript pages in particular T20635 to 7. And, Your Honours, to have a look at the chronology that has been prepared for Your Honours where you can see the events set out across each municipality, in particular, as we commend to Your Honours what you can see on pages 28 and 29. We would have put it up, but it's -- it's too big. Your Honours, the size of the operation required, as we say, control and coordination between the political authorities, the police, and the military. We say the evidence shows it required it, and it got it through the regional level of authority headed by Radoslav Brdjanin. And finally, Your Honours, so that one can see in visual form the implementation we say of the plan, can I just very quickly put up the maps that were prepared showing the various forms of destruction. Can I start with the killing sites, which is Exhibit P2650. Your Honour, these are dealing with the killings connected with the detention camps, the two coloured dots refer to the different types. And as one can see, and I repeat, Your Honour, that is why we suggest the Defence is so anxious to say these were renegade municipalities, the worst -- the largest numbers occurred in Prijedor, in Sanski Most, in Kljuc, Kotor Varos doesn't get a mention, and up in Novi. Thank you. Then next, could we look, please, at the exhumation sites, because that gives us some idea of how difficult it was to recover the bodies. This is P2648. As Your Honour knows, even today, as you heard Mr. Biscevic say a few minutes ago, many bodies have not been recovered. Your Honours heard, and we've set it out in the final brief, the number of bodies that have been recovered and from which sites. Perhaps the most unanswered question of this whole period in this area is where the bodies are of the men who were killed in the Grabovica school. Yes, thank you. Your Honours, can we then look, please, briefly as I say again at P2649, which is where the camps were situated. And there, we can see that each and every municipality, with the exception of Celinac, for reasons which I think we'll come to tomorrow, had its camps. The largest number, again, in Prijedor. Thank you. And finally, P2647, the destruction of religious or the damage, destruction, to religious property. Not one municipality escaped. In Banja Luka, it's right to say that the major destruction took place in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 1993, the destruction took place in 1993. In 1992, it was pure -- it was merely damage, if that can be put that way, as "merely." Your Honour, one can see, we suggest, from this map why Dr. Kaiser, when he gave evidence, the expert, described this as a systematic approach to the destruction. Yes, thank you. Your Honour, I was going to deal, in fact, because it led into the genocide thing, but I will leave that until tomorrow, the few words I want to say about genocide, once we have dealt with the question that Your Honour has. I want to deal briefly if I may before I come on to Mr. Brdjanin himself, the question of media and propaganda in general terms. Your Honour, in order to persuade the ordinary Serbs of the threat, the so-called threat, posed to them by their Muslim and Croat neighbours with whom they were living up until 1991 on good terms, that they had to make sure, the Serbs, that the propaganda went out as far as was possible unopposed by the propaganda which we accept entirely was being put out on behalf of the Muslim and Croat populations. And also, to ensure that their official pronouncements were circulated not only as and when required, but also accurately. Your Honour, we say that the evidence shows that within the Autonomous Region of Krajina, this accused, Mr. Brdjanin, together with his cohort, Dr. Vukic, of the SDS, were the leading proponents of the strategy of -- to try and take control of the media. Your Honour, we have already dealt with the takeover of the Kozara transmitter by Veljko Milankovic's group. And according to witnesses, this did cause an enormous change in the type of programming because the programmes they were receiving came not any more from Sarajevo, but from Belgrade and Novi Sad. Your Honour, on the 6th of March 1992, there was a press conference when Vukic made a statement about Radio Banja Luka stressing that the editorial policy to date has not served sufficiently the interests of the ruling party and that it should be changed as soon as possible. And about ten days later, he said that Radio Banja Luka should broadcast reports from the battlefield every day. Your Honours may recall that there was a witness who dealt with the events of Banja Luka -- sorry, Banja Luka Radio at some length, and I'm not going to go into that. But Your Honour, one of the things that the Defence have said in their response, and this is at page 2, they say "there is no evidence of the Autonomous Region of Krajina Crisis Staff or Radoslav Brdjanin giving instructions to radio stations." Well, I suppose if you read that simply as Banja Luka Radio must do this, that is right. But from its beginnings, it issued decisions and conclusions concerning the media. On the 6th of May 1992, the media, in the autonomous region, are to furnish maximum information. Your Honour, I should say all of what I'm now going to read comes from P227, the Gazettes. On the 8th of May 1992: "In future, Krajina media are to operate according to wartime schedules." And what does that mean? "That is, they must promptly inform all citizens about all orders and decisions of the war staff of the ARK." On the 18th of May, because you can issue whatever orders you want, but if the technical equipment is not working, they sent -- they said that "TV Banja Luka is to send technicians immediately to maintain the relay at Vlasic." So there we have a direct order to the actual station itself. And then on the 4th of June, the announcement of the establishment of the radio/television Krajina. And Your Honour, the many documents which have come from the Banja Luka railway station -- railway station. Television station and radio station -- I'm sorry, radio station, do show that those decisions were being read out as requested, apart from what we see in the newspapers, because you have the actual copy of the decision of the crisis staffs with the radio announcer's written -- when it's to be played and who is going to deal with it. Your Honour, the municipal crisis staffs also played their part in implementing the instructions that they were getting about the -- from the ARK about radio programming. Petrovac, on the 18th of June 1992, it sent a clear direction on the type of programme to be broadcast. That is Exhibit 1834. And on the subject of the type of propaganda that was being broadcast, if one looks at Exhibit 1811, they were broadcasting an announcement starting "Serbs, and all upstanding people of Krajina, let us stem the tide of fascism. Our houses, towns, and villages are again being torched and destroyed. We are fighting against Ustasha and Islamic fascists." It makes the point, Your Honour, very clearly: You have to terrify your people into believing that you are going -- that they are being attacked by the Ustasha and Islamic fascists in order to persuade them either to condone or to take part in the crimes that are going to be committed. And the radio stations were vital, as Your Honours know, in broadcasting the demands for the surrender of the weapons and for the surrender of people. In Kljuc, with the incident in the Pudin Han area, when Omer Filipovic was being ordered to surrender, when he had gone to negotiate. And in P28 -- I'm sorry, P928, which again was Kljuc Radio -- I'm sorry, again it was Kljuc Radio of the 29th of May 1992, and for some reason we can get that up. This was one of the ultimatums being issued in respect of Kljuc, and we see there: "We hope that the leadership of the so-called Muslim Territorial Defence has finally realised that what it is doing is political and real suicide of its own people. In other words, a crime against its own people against which it has no right, and we hope the attack is on the police patrol" and so on and so forth. Your Honour, Glas was perhaps the only newspaper that was not fully at all times subservient to the wishes of its political masters, and it may well be that that came about because Mr. Mladjenovic who was the editor was a close associate - he had been a member of the ARK Assembly and had been concerned with the takeover of Kozara - of the governing bodies, the men on the governing bodies. But even he went one step too far. He wrote in March of 1992 an article entitled "all authority is from God," and, Your Honour, that is Exhibit P482. And in that article, he stated that he had no intention of editing the newspaper of the SDS except in a context that would ensure the mutual respect of all nations. So on the 7th of July, the Banja Luka War Presidency dismissed Mladjenovic. On the 11th of July, Glas published a report on a press conference that was given by Brdjanin and Kupresanin, and one that was given on the same day by the SDS Municipal Board with dealt with the dismissal of Mr. Mladjenovic. And it was stated that this was a decision of the ARK Crisis Staff, confirmed by the Banja Luka Municipal Assembly. And on the 17th of July, at a meeting of the municipal assembly, again, according to Glas, Radic confirmed that indeed the original decision had been made at the ARK War Presidency meeting. Your Honour, those exhibit numbers are Exhibit P498 and 2696. Your Honour, Mr. Radic, indeed, when he gave evidence, went slightly round the houses about this matter, but you will recall there was this long discussion because he was saying he had taken -- he had no minutes, but he was apparently waving minutes at the session of the municipal assembly relating to the ARK Crisis Staff. Your Honours, we're going to come on to what we say Mr. Brdjanin's part in all of this was. But we say that one of the -- one of the major ways that he promoted the goals of the Serb leadership was not only by the decisions he made as head of the organisations, of which he was the head, in particular the crisis staff, but by his inflammatory speeches. Mr. Radic said: "As deputy and as president of the crisis staff, he had access to the media, to the TV, to the newspapers, to the radio." Your Honour, that's at page 22308. In our final brief, we added this comment, that he only had this access because the media was strictly controlled and used as a tool of the Serb leadership. That again, has attracted criticism from the Defence who state in their -- I think it must be their response, at page 2, that common sense tells us that politicians everywhere have media access irrespective of media control. Well, I don't know, Your Honour, whether common sense would tell us that or whether some of the politicians might complain that unfair access was provided. But that, Your Honour, with respect, is not the point. The point is whether politicians everywhere may or may not have that. The ARK Crisis Staff and the municipal crisis staff were doing their best to ensure by a series of decisions and orders and their power to remove the editors of newspapers, not to mention the editors of television programmes, if they were not going to follow the instructions that were being given to them. Your Honour, it wasn't just TV -- well, Your Honour, I see the time. There were two documents I want to look at, but I'll deal with that tomorrow and then move to Mr. Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just want you to know that even though the next two days are reserved for the Defence, that we have, because of the delays on the first day, on Monday, we have yielded the first session tomorrow, an hour and a half of our time, to Ms. Korner just as a matter of fairness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. But would the rest be enough for your purposes?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: We think it will be, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, okay. We have in the meantime, between -- since yesterday discussed amongst ourselves the merits of your two motions, the one to strike off the entire final brief of the Prosecution, and the other one, to strike off Appendix C. We will be handing down our decision first thing tomorrow morning when we reconvene. However, we thought it fit to tell you what the decisions are so that both of you will be prepared. Ms. Korner, because she will be concluding her submissions, and you, because you have to start. Both will be oral decisions. We're trying to economise on resources at this present moment, and I'm trying to have my staff -- our staff concentrate on several issues related to this case. Both motions are going to be rejected. However, there will be reasons given, and also statements regarding some of your allegations and what the consequences of your submissions ought to be in the view of the Trial Chamber. But that would put you both in the picture as far as -- yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm taking it that won't be, though, until the speeches are concluded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no. You will finish your closing argument now.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And then there will be the decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. In England, we call them closing speeches.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Closing speeches, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So Your Honours will give the ruling at the end of both --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We can give the ruling straight away when we start tomorrow morning. But I don't want to take any of your time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, that's what I was going to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is the whole issue. So basically, you are both advised what the conclusions are going to be. And then it's not that much important as to the timing when the oral decisions will be handed down. But they will be handed down tomorrow. Okay? Thank you.
